topic: Sharp finite-plate hierarchical ATE bounds: observe n independent clusters, each with exactly fixed m conditionally iid binary exposure-outcome pairs generated from a latent four-cell law q with positivity epsilon, latent ignorability given q, and unknown mixing law mu; only each cluster's multinomial count is observed. For every b in the relative interior of the feasible degree-m Bernstein moment body, characterize the sharp cluster-equally-weighted ATE interval as an attained generalized-moment primal and Bernstein-polynomial dual with no gap; prove endpoint compatible hierarchical SCMs need at most N_m=binom(m+3,3) atoms; prove universal point identification iff the nonlinear ATE functional lies in the affine Bernstein span and hence fails for every finite m; give a terminating CAD recovery-or-endpoint-witness procedure for rational inputs and uniform whole-identified-set coverage by simultaneous multinomial-region inversion. Consumer: the JRSS C 2023 São Paulo directly-observed-therapy versus binary-cure analysis, whose ATE posteriors change with city random-effect specification.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp cluster-equally-weighted ATE interval when a fixed-size cluster count reveals only degree-m multinomial Bernstein moments of an unrestricted mixing law over positive four-cell exposure-outcome probabilities, including the smallest universal endpoint-support cap.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Wood treats one-dimensional binomial mixing, the generalized-moment papers treat noncausal objectives, and the prior SCM proposal obtains attainment only after fixing a finite latent alphabet. None supplies the four-cell conditional-ignorability ATE specialization. The first missing steps are to identify the cluster-count law with the constrained degree-m Bernstein moment map, prove weak compactness and exclude a vertical supporting hyperplane at relative-interior b, and compress an endpoint measure on the dual contact face rather than in the larger ambient graph; the last distinction is needed for the binom(m+3,3) atom count and for conversion back to compatible hierarchical SCMs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An attained measure-valued minimization/maximization formula for both ATE endpoints, an equal-valued attained Bernstein-polynomial majorant/minorant dual, and endpoint-compatible hierarchical SCMs supported on at most binom(m+3,3) latent laws, with a contact-rank refinement if possible.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Finite-m nonuniqueness of the mixing law does not imply variation of this particular causal functional on every fiber: the ATE could accidentally be constant on a nontrivial fiber. The missing argument must turn relative-interior feasibility into a full-support representing law and then construct a signed perturbation annihilating every Bernstein coordinate but not the ATE, dominated in both signs by that law. Existing mixture papers establish mixing-law nonidentification, the GMP result supplies broader strict feasibility, and the prior proposals distinguish generic rank failure from genuine nonidentification, but none proves this every-interior-fiber statement or classifies boundary collapse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient affine-span criterion for universal ATE point identification, a strict-positive-width theorem furnishing two compatible SCMs for every relative-interior fiber outside that span, and a semialgebraic characterization or counterexample catalogue for zero-width boundary fibers.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a strictly feasible representing measure from relative-interior moment data and use moment-cone separation to obtain dual attainment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Strict ATE width requires perturbing a representative in both signs while preserving Bernstein moments; strict feasibility supplies the interior slack needed for domination.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze finite-moment fibers through the convex hull of a binomial likelihood curve and distinguish unique from nonunique mixture representations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The multinomial Bernstein body is the higher-dimensional analogue, while the target asks whether one nonlinear scalar is constant on its fibers.

open_problems.why_unsolved: AutoBounds offers numerical global optimization for finite discrete response types, while the hierarchical problem optimizes over an unrestricted measure on a continuous simplex; symbolic causal-bound work likewise guarantees sharpness only for narrower finite-dimensional classes. The prior LiNGAM run shows how CAD can stratify polynomial moment systems, but the first proof step here must establish the atomic support cap before elimination, clear the rational ATE denominators using positivity, encode primal-dual contact, and rule out spurious cleared-denominator roots while mapping every solution back to a compatible hierarchical SCM.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A correctness-and-termination theorem for CAD or real quantifier elimination that outputs minimal polynomials and isolating intervals for both endpoints, at-most-binom(m+3,3)-atom SCM realizations, and matching Bernstein dual certificates, or an exact infeasibility certificate, with a worked rational m=2 interior instance.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic partial-identification procedures typically start from estimable bound functions or finite moment inequalities, but each endpoint here is itself an infinite-dimensional measure optimization and is nonsmooth when its dual contact set changes. The prior data-fusion run records the analogous unresolved coverage problem at ties. The needed proof must show that inverting one simultaneous multinomial region before optimization covers every compatible Bernstein vector and therefore its whole ATE fiber uniformly, including sequences where the true interval collapses; endpoint delta methods and pointwise mixing-distribution intervals do not establish that whole-set statement.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample or asymptotically uniform 1-alpha confidence set C_n equal to the union of sharp ATE fibers over a simultaneous multinomial region, with uniform whole-identified-set coverage over all admissible mixing laws and an explicit width result covering boundary and tie sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its focus on why inference must remain valid as the width of an identified interval changes, with fixed-plate fibers supplying the new nonregular geometry.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The target is an interval rather than a point -> its width can shrink to zero on boundary sequences -> endpoint-wise asymptotics can lose uniform coverage -> invert an observable-law region and cover the entire hierarchical ATE fiber

method_exemplars.technique: Prove uniform identified-set coverage by test inversion while controlling discontinuities from changing binding moment restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Changing dual contact sets play the role of changing active inequalities, so the same uniformity obstacle must be controlled.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a simultaneous multinomial region jointly calibrated for all count-cell probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The empirical input is one multinomial law over cluster-count configurations; mapping a joint region through the sharp fiber avoids differentiating nonsmooth endpoints.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact composite tests against least-favorable observationally equivalent mixing laws using stochastic monotonicity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates exact inversion under the same fixed-plate information loss, although for univariate mixing CDFs and quantiles rather than a multivariate causal-functional fiber.

open_problems.open_problem: As fixed plate size m grows, determine the sharp decay rate of the maximal interior ATE-fiber width and whether it equals, up to explicit constants or exactly, the best uniform degree-m affine-Bernstein approximation error for the four-cell ATE functional.

source_refs.excerpt: pair it with the published moment-matching lower bound

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted source pairs polynomial approximation with moment-matched lower priors for the same rational four-cell ATE functional, but it studies sampling risk across discrete confounder cells rather than information loss from a multinomial plate. The first proof step that changes is a multivariate inverse moment argument: uniformly approximate the ATE by the affine Bernstein span for an upper width bound, then construct two positive mixing laws that match every degree-m Bernstein coordinate while attaining the approximation residual. Maintaining a prescribed relative-interior b, rather than merely matching two arbitrary laws, is the additional unresolved constraint.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact equality or matching two-sided asymptotic bound relating the supremum over relative-interior b of U_m(b)-L_m(b) to the best uniform affine-Bernstein approximation error of the ATE functional, with moment-matched mixing laws attaining the lower rate.

method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite-plate fiber width is governed by the component of the same ATE functional invisible to all degree-m moments.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Basu et al. establish a bounded-versus-growing trial-size contrast for univariate mixing-distribution functionals, and Wood-Lai-Qiao target only a linear latent mean. The scan found no result for the nonlinear causal ATE of a four-cell law under a distribution of multinomial plate sizes. The first proof step that changes from fixed m is that the observable function system becomes the union of Bernstein spaces indexed by plate size; one must determine when that union separates the ATE functional or approximates it uniformly under positivity, and then convert the approximation residual into a sharp fiber-width rate while accounting for the frequency of informative sizes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient condition on the support and sampling frequency of plate sizes for ATE identification, together with explicit upper and lower rates for the worst-case sharp-interval width as the largest informative plate size tends to infinity.

writing_exemplar.why: Its bounded-versus-growing plate-size contrast gives the cleanest motivation arc for an information frontier rather than another random-effects model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Each bounded plate reveals finitely many mixing moments -> infinitely many groups do not remove finite-order aliasing -> larger plate sizes enlarge the observable Bernstein system -> characterize when that system identifies the hierarchical ATE and how fast its fiber shrinks

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit multiple binomial sample sizes to recover a functional of a common mixing distribution and track the moment information contributed by each size.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem also pools heterogeneous plate sizes, but replaces a linear latent success mean with the nonlinear four-cell ATE.

method_exemplars.technique: Use equality of finite moment sequences to construct observational equivalence under bounded plate sizes and contrast it with increasing-size recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same moment aliasing supplies the lower-bound side of the varying-plate ATE identification frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate latent mixing structure through a known binomial observation kernel using finite-dimensional exponential-family g-modeling and derive uncertainty through the fitted marginal model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once growing plates provide approximate identification, the hierarchical multinomial likelihood becomes a known-kernel deconvolution problem with a concrete regularized estimator.

literature_map:
Nobre, Schmidt, Moodie, and Stephens (2023, JRSS C; arXiv:2304.12548) estimate the São Paulo DOT-on-cure ATE with Bayesian city random effects and show substantial posterior movement across latent-structure specifications.
Wood (1999, Annals of Statistics, doi:10.1214/aos/1017939148) describes fixed-size binomial mixtures through finite moments and convex geometry, with nonunique mixing representations.
Wood, Lai, and Qiao (2005, ANZJS, doi:10.1111/j.1467-842X.2005.00407.x) exploit varying binomial trial sizes for a linear mean functional, leaving nonlinear four-cell causal functionals untreated.
Basu, Brill, and Yekutieli (2026, JCGS; arXiv:2311.14424) construct exact test-inversion intervals for mixing CDFs and quantiles and document information loss under bounded plate sizes.
Diaconis and Freedman (1980, Annals of Probability, doi:10.1214/aop/1176994663) give the foundational finite-exchangeability comparison with mixtures of iid laws, but not sharp causal-functional bounds.
Bertsimas and Popescu (2005, SIAM Journal on Optimization, doi:10.1137/S1052623401399903) supply the generalized-moment primal-dual template for sharp expectations under finite moments.
Bayer and Teichmann (2006, Proceedings AMS; arXiv:math/0502473) prove finite atomic cubature representations bounded by the dimension of the moment function system.
Halaseh, Magron, and Skomra (2026; arXiv:2604.15072) prove dual attainment and strict-feasibility results for compact polynomial generalized moment problems under relative-interior hypotheses.
Duarte et al. (2023, JASA; arXiv:2109.13471) automate numerical sharp causal bounds through polynomial programming, branch-and-bound, and epsilon-sharp certificates.
Sachs et al. (2022, JCGS; arXiv:2003.10702) derive symbolic causal bounds for finite discrete latent-response models, but their guaranteed-tight class does not cover unrestricted continuous mixing measures.
England, Bradford, and Davenport (2020, Journal of Symbolic Computation; arXiv:1903.08999) provide equational-constraint-aware CAD machinery suitable for exact semialgebraic endpoint recovery after finite-support reduction.
Imbens-Manski (2004), Stoye (2009), and Bugni (2010) show why interval and identified-set inference must handle nonuniformity as widths or active constraints change.
Sison and Glaz (1995, JASA, doi:10.1080/01621459.1995.10476521) provide simultaneous multinomial coverage that can be inverted before applying a nonsmooth sharp-bound map.
Across targeted searches, no paper combined a fixed multinomial plate, unrestricted four-cell mixing law, conditional latent ignorability, and sharp nonparametric ATE fiber; the live tension is between model-dependent hierarchical posteriors and finite-moment-compatible causal identified sets.
